response.query: Which quasi-experimental methods (propensity score matching, difference-in-differences, regression discontinuity) are feasible with short-panel or cross-sectional student data to improve causal claims?
response.answer: Propensity score matching and regression discontinuity are feasible with short-panel or cross-sectional student data to improve causal claims. Difference-in-differences is less suitable for short-panel data.

results.title: Schooling and entrepreneurship: Evidence from a ...
results.content: # Schooling and entrepreneurship: Evidence from a regression discontinuity design☆. A Regression Discontinuity Design is used to obtain causal estimates of the relationship between high school education and adult entrepreneurship. Estimates indicate a negative relationship between an additional year of schooling and engagement in self-employment. The findings cast doubt on the notion that the additional schooling affected self-employment through productivity or credentialing channels. Policy implications might be most applicable to developing countries where governments are exploring whether to raise school leaving ages. To test the mechanisms and uncover whether there are causal relationships between these variables, we exploit two exogenous changes to British compulsory schooling laws that generated sharp across-cohort differences in years of education. Using a fuzzy regression discontinuity design, we estimate that the reforms significantly reduced self-employment. ## Data availability. The authors do not have permission to share data. Full responsibility for the editorial process for this article was delegated to another journal editor.
